payload.rationale: Seattle enters as the stronger roster on background: the Seahawks were the NFL's top team in 2025 (Super Bowl champions with an elite defense), while Arizona was a losing team in 2025 and remains a lower-tier roster despite an encouraging 26-14 Week 1 win. Under normal conditions Seattle would be a modest road favorite in Glendale. However, the supplied injury report lists Seattle QB Sam Darnold as OUT, forcing a backup starter (likely Drew Lock or Jalen Milroe), which historically costs a team roughly 3-6 points of expected margin. Combined with Arizona's home field (~1.5-2 points), this pushes the matchup close to even. Arizona also has notable injury questions (CB Garrett Williams out; several linemen and secondary players questionable), which partially offsets. Week 1 results (Seattle 13-10, Arizona 26-14) are a tiny sample and I weight them lightly. Net: roughly a pick'em with a slight edge to Seattle's superior defense and overall talent, giving Arizona about 47%. Too high if Seattle's backup QB is competent enough behind an elite defense to still control the game, and Arizona's Week 1 win overstates its quality. Too low if Arizona's home crowd and the loss of Seattle's starting QB matter more than modeled, or if Arizona has genuinely improved under a new-look 2026 roster. A tie (~0.4%) resolves at $0.50, not YES.
limitations: Only one game of 2026 data; no opponent-adjusted team ratings supplied.
Seattle's backup QB identity and quality are not supplied; the size of the Darnold-absence effect is an assumption.
Final game-day inactives may differ from the Friday report.
Background knowledge of 2026 rosters and coaching changes may be incomplete.
